Subject: Redwood data residency questions for NB-RFP-2027-042

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this RFP — Novabank (NB) has a short list of clarifying questions on data residency and regional availability that we need to include in our controls appendix. These are focused on production traffic, telemetry, and short-lived caches. Please see the attached spreadsheet with the items where we need straight yes/no plus short evidence links. High-level asks below:

1) Can Redwood guarantee that all production inference requests and model state (KV caches, request logs) for an EU tenant remain within EU regions (EU-WEST/Dublin, EU-CENTRAL/Frankfurt) by default? If not, under what conditions do you permit cross-border processing?

2) If a regional outage occurs, what is the failover order and what contractual opt-ins are required for failover to non-EU regions? Do you support customer-only EU routing (no cross-border failover) as a hard lock?

3) For short-lived caching (prefix/KV caches and pre-warm caches), do you ever persist or warm caches outside the tenant's home region? Please describe TTLs and eviction behavior that could lead to cross-border replication.

4) Auditing/evidence: we need a time-bound attestation (signed) confirming deployment footprint and a sample trace showing region of execution for tokens across three requests. SOC 2 and network flow logs would be helpful.

We are concentrating on EU production for now; please advise deliverables and ETA for the responses and any redlines you foresee. Our procurement team would like the finalized answers by EOD 24-May to include in the binder.

Best,
Marta
Director, Cloud Procurement
NovaBank

Subject: [Internal Draft] Proposed answers to NB residency questions

Team — internal draft answers below (marked [Draft]). These are operationally accurate but will need a short cover note and a link to the SOC2 evidence before sending externally. I also flagged one item (cache cross-border) that may require a contractual opt-in if they require absolute prevention.

[DRAFT ANSWERS]
1) EU-only processing: Default behavior is tenant-bound placement in the customer's selected home region(s). For EU-tenants we deploy to EU-CENTRAL (Frankfurt) and EU-WEST (Dublin) only unless the customer explicitly opts into cross-region replication or we perform emergency failover. We cannot offer 100% technical immutability for ephemeral caches without an annex — our runtime may pre-warm in adjacent regions to reduce cold-starts unless isolated.

2) Failover order & opt-ins: Failover order is: primary region -> secondary EU region -> controlled failover to a geo-pair (e.g., UK or US-WEST) ONLY with written escalation and a defined SLA exception. Customers can choose a "strict residency" option (contract-level) that prevents cross-border failover; this may increase latency and reduce availability guarantees by design.

3) Caching behaviour: Prefix/KV cache TTL default is 5 minutes for short-lived caches and 24 hours for pre-warm artifacts. Ephemeral caches are not persisted to object stores. Pre-warm artifacts may be staged in a neighbouring region for performance; we can scope policy to disallow this for customers who select strict residency.

4) Evidence & attestation: We can provide: (a) SOC 2 Type II report redacted for public distribution; (b) per-request execution traces showing region flags and IP of serving node; (c) time-bound signed attestation of deployment footprint. Estimated ETA to produce these artifacts: 3 business days once scope confirmed.

Attachments: data_residency_draft_answers.docx (internal).

Notes for Soojin: highlight the strict-residency opt-in and the potential tradeoffs (latency/availability) to the customer; Laura — please draft the attestation template for signature.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Product Manager, Platform

Hi Marta (and NB procurement),

Appended are our formal responses to the residency questions you sent. Key points up front:

- Default placement: EU tenants are hosted in EU-CENTRAL (Frankfurt) and/or EU-WEST (Dublin) depending on capacity and customer preference. Production inference requests, logs, and persistent artifacts are kept within those EU regions by default.

- Emergency failover: Our standard failover path is primary EU region -> secondary EU region. Cross-border failover to non-EU (e.g., US-WEST) occurs only under explicit contractual opt-in ("Failover Authorization") and after automatic routing attempts to EU fall back to secondary EU targets. Customers may select a "Strict Residency" hosting annex that prohibits cross-border failover entirely; note this may affect availability SLOs.

- Caches & pre-warm artifacts: Short-lived KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and kept in-region by default. Pre-warm artifacts (used to reduce cold-starts) may be staged in an adjacent EU zone for performance; we can disable staging for customers who require strict residency. Default TTLs: short-lived caches = 5 minutes; pre-warm = 24 hours (configurable).

- Evidence and attestation: Attached PDF includes: (1) signed deployment footprint attestation template; (2) sample request traces showing execution region headers; (3) list of audit artifacts we can provide (SOC2 Type II link, flow logs, per-request region flags). Estimated delivery for full evidence package: within 3 business days after confirmation of the scope (prod only vs prod+non-prod).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the residency guarantees are required for production only or also for non-prod/staging.
2) Confirm if you require the Strict Residency annex (if yes, we'll include the appendix and note the availability tradeoffs).
3) If you want a short call to walk the artifacts, I'm available Friday 21-May 16:00 CET.

Attachments: Novabank_Redwood_DataResidency_Response_v1.pdf

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the thorough response and the PDF — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications before we finalize the binder:

1) Cache staging: can you confirm whether pre-warm staging to an adjacent EU zone ever writes to persistent storage outside the EU? We need confirmation that no cache artifacts (even pre-warm blobs) are persisted outside the EU unless a customer signs the Failover Authorization.

2) Failover Authorization: procurement is open to a narrow failover authorization but would like the contract to require Redwood to use EU-only fallback targets first for 30 minutes, and only then escalate to non-EU targets with automated alerts + pre-approved escalation contact list. Is that operationally feasible?

3) We will need a signed attestation for the production footprint (single-page) attached to the procurement bundle. Can you confirm you will deliver the signed attestation and SOC2 link by EOD 26-May?

If possible, please return a short confirmatory email that we can include verbatim in the binder. Procurement will follow up on the hosting annex/DocuSign link once the technicals are confirmed.
